_doc: Routing, cost and quota constants for the orchestrator loop (docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-orchestrator-loop.md sections 8 and 9). Read by budget.py and plan_wave.py. A constant changes only by an explicit edit that restates its date and source.

calibration.source: REFIT 2026-10-07 from the first two meter readings of ONE account inside ONE session window (kb/Work PB2478; design D6/D7): account 2 read week 0 % / session 0 % at 13:26-13:34 PDT and week 6 % / session 24 % at 14:54 PDT (session window 10:09-15:09); its OWN telemetry between them (user.account_uuid filtered) counted 9,481,140 Opus, 108,118 Sonnet and 646,023 Haiku tokens of the counted kinds ($177 of Opus). The 2026-10-04 constants (Opus 400,000 per point, fitted to the Workflow tool's subagent token counts, not to telemetry) made that 25.4 points and a 127 % session, and held the loop while the meter read 6 % and 24 %. The refit is the old rates times 4 (Opus 1.6 M; 9.48 M / 1.6 M + the rest = 6.0 points), every ratio between families kept; the per-group and lander token costs below are scaled by the same 4 so a planned wave costs the same points as before. Refit again whenever two readings of one account bracket a measured spend.
calibration.tokens_per_point_frontier_source: fable and mythos: 2.5x the Opus rate, the published price ratio ($10/$50 against $4/$20 per MTok; kb/Work R69, 2026-10-06), until a meter reading refits it; haiku: a third of the Sonnet rate's cost, the published price ratio ($1/$5 against $3/$15 per MTok; 2026-10-07), where it was priced at the Opus fallback before
calibration.session_pct_per_weekly_pct_source: measured 2026-10-07 (kb/Work PB2478): account 2's session moved 0 -> 24 % while its week moved 0 -> 6 % inside one session window (13:34 -> 14:54 PDT); the 5.0 before was a guess (design D7)

accounts._doc: The Claude accounts the loop runs from (owner 2026-10-07 13:17 PDT: the OPERATOR session on a second Max 20x account, the Mythos work on the first; kb/Work PB2478). account.py resolves the running account from CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (unset = the row whose config_dir is null); a config dir no row names is an error. Each row: name, config_dir (~ expands; null = ~/.claude), weekly_reset (Python weekday(): Monday 0 ... Sunday 6), and optionally `quota` keys that differ from the shared quota below. budget.py stamps every reading with the account and reads only that account's readings and telemetry (user.account_uuid).

seed._doc: What a named account's config dir carries (kb/Work PB2480): scripts/account-profile.ps1 makes it so, account.py --seed-check (and tooling_check.py at every session start) verifies it. `copy`: taken from the default account's dir when missing (a directory: each missing child); `junction`: the default account's folder, linked so both accounts share it ({repo_key} = the main checkout's projects key); `flags`: non-secret feature flags set in the account's .claude.json (Claude in Chrome on: the meter unit reads the usage page through it). `never`: credentials are never copied, the owner signs the account in (/login).

quota.weekly_cap_source: owner 2026-10-07 09:40 PDT: "raise session and weekly quota limits to 97%" (kb/Work R69 section 6); it replaced the 85 % cap of the same morning (06:00), which had replaced the 98 % ceiling of 2026-10-02 and the 44 % cap on other work of 2026-10-05. Owner 10:15 PDT: "You can push it to 100% as long as you do not cause any work to abort due to lack of quota" — 100 is the CEILING; 97 is the DISPATCH cap, 100 minus the margin one wave's estimate can be wrong by (tokens_per_point and session_pct_per_weekly_pct are unrefit guesses), so what is in flight at 97 finishes inside the quota instead of dying at 100. Refitting the estimator shrinks the margin; the ceiling does not move
quota.session_stop_source: owner 2026-10-07 09:40 PDT: the session limit is 97 % (the soft stop, where dispatching holds and in-flight agents checkpoint); the hard stop stays two points above it so a hold always precedes a kill; before that 70/90 from the 2026-10-04 design (kb/Work PB1981)

routing._owner_approval_why: A note whose body says its work needs a frontier model (Fable, Mythos) under the owner's approval is never planned: that approval is per dispatch (MANDATORY-PRACTICES P1), which an unattended wave cannot obtain, so the planner lists the note as waiting and the attended session asks. First case: PB2118, R1's authorship (kb/Work R69 section 4, PB2120, 2026-10-07).
routing._why: Opus where the work is design-heavy (OO, grammar), where a note says a design question is open, or where a note has already failed twice (a note that fails twice is a task-spec problem, kb/Work PB1981). Opus also for the legacy-retirement cuts (CI and gate wiring carry the CI invariant) and the architecture review's R0/R1 items (kb/Work R69). Fable and Mythos are never values here: each needs explicit owner approval per dispatch (owner 2026-10-02; R69 2026-10-06).

cost.source: seeded 2026-10-04 so that a five-note group costs about 0.4 weekly points on either model, a lander about 0.3, and a six-group wave of five-note groups about 3 points with its landers, matching waves 1011-1015 (kb/Work PB1981: a six-group wave already costs about 3 weekly points); refit from units.jsonl. Scaled x4 on 2026-10-07 with tokens_per_point (kb/Work PB2478), so the points a group costs are unchanged

campaign._why: plan_wave.py --cluster (kb/Work PB2120): a campaign note's code sites are whatever it names, so its notes are clustered over the whole tree, not .agent-fleet.json's src/Cobol.Net.* (which the fix lane keeps). Project files (.csproj, .props, .targets) are not sites: their dotted names (Cobol.Net.Cli.csproj) make fix_clusters read every `Cobol.Net` in a note as a Type.Member reference to the first one indexed (measured on PB2108, 2026-10-07). exclude_dir names directories that hold corpora or generated output, never a fix site: the GnuCOBOL corpus (tests/external), the conformance programs and goldens, gate run output, and the frozen evidence records under docs/.

wave.max_groups_source: waves 1011-1015 ran 5 to 7 groups; the budget is the governor, this bounds the train count
